ModuleIndex

Offline ELF and DWARF API in namespace tracer_module. Substituting the first-probe ELF and using new output paths, build an index and set auto hit = idx.find_symbol("add(int, int)"); for examples that require a symbol ID.

Source declarations.

Methods: build · open · path · identity · types · symbols · find_type · find_symbol · get_type · get_symbol · emit_headers · prepare_probe

ModuleIndex build

build(source, output, options={})

Create a new SQLite module index; optional budgets and cancellation apply.

cpp
auto idx = tracer_module::ModuleIndex::build(tracer_module::ModuleSource::file("./target"), "target.sqlite");
ModuleIndex open

open(path)

Open an existing local index without changing the REPL selection.

cpp
auto idx = tracer_module::ModuleIndex::open("target.sqlite");
ModuleIndex path

path()

Return the index file path.

cpp
std::cout << idx.path();
ModuleIndex identity

identity()

Read ELF and debug identity and indexing diagnostics.

cpp
std::cout << idx.identity().build_id;
ModuleIndex types

types(query={})

Return indexed types and an optional next-page token.

cpp
tracer_module::ModuleQuery q; q.filter = "int"; auto page = idx.types(q);
ModuleIndex symbols

symbols(query={})

Return indexed symbols, optionally only dynamic exports.

cpp
auto page = idx.symbols(tracer_module::SymbolQuery{}.exported_only());
ModuleIndex find_type

find_type(name)

Find a uniquely named type.

cpp
auto type = idx.find_type("int");
ModuleIndex find_symbol

find_symbol(name)

Resolve an unambiguous selector, linkage name, or name.

cpp
auto hit = idx.find_symbol("add(int, int)");
ModuleIndex get_type

get_type(id)

Read a type by stable ID from this index.

cpp
auto type = idx.get_type(idx.find_type("int").id);
ModuleIndex get_symbol

get_symbol(id)

Read a symbol by stable ID from this index.

cpp
auto symbol = idx.get_symbol(hit.id);
ModuleIndex emit_headers

emit_headers(selection, output)

Write recovered declarations, views and manifest to a new directory.

cpp
idx.emit_headers({{hit.id}, {}}, "recovered");
ModuleIndex prepare_probe

prepare_probe(symbol_id, module, output, generated={}, metadata_only=false)

Make an indexed package for that symbol. Empty module uses the recorded ELF. A supplied generated bundle is verified; metadata_only skips separate adapter files.

cpp
idx.prepare_probe(hit.id, {}, "prepared", "recovered");

Module index inputs and results

These options and results belong to the offline module index; ELF addresses are relative to the image.

Source declarations.

  • ModuleSource: image, debug_file, expected_build_id.
  • ModuleIndexOptions: max_entries, max_depth (zero leaves the bound open), cancelled predicate.
  • ModuleQuery: filter glob, page continuation, limit (zero reads all); SymbolQuery adds exports.
  • ModulePage<Entry>: entries and next_page. Keep the query filters unchanged when using the next token.
  • ModuleSelection: symbols and types are ID lists.
  • ModuleIdentity provides image and debug paths, digests, build ID, and diagnostics. ModuleType and ModuleField describe recovered types, sizes, fields and offsets. ModuleSymbol and ModuleParameter describe callable identity, source, return type and parameter type IDs. See the declarations linked above for every field.

Methods: file · exported_only

Module index inputs and results file

ModuleSource::file(image, debug_file={})

Describe an ELF with an optional matching separate debug file.

cpp
auto source = tracer_module::ModuleSource::file("./target", "./target.debug");
Module index inputs and results exported_only

SymbolQuery::exported_only()

Set the dynamic-export filter and return the query by reference.

cpp
tracer_module::SymbolQuery q; q.exported_only();

Launch checkpoint

An opt-in checkpoint in target application code. Use it with owned launch and registered calls.

Source declarations.

Methods: wait_for_resume · named_call

Launch checkpoint wait_for_resume

wait_for_resume(); wait_for_resume(calls...)

Pause at the launch gate and service registered calls before resume. Check the boolean result before continuing startup.

cpp
if (!tracer::launch::wait_for_resume()) return 1;
Launch checkpoint named_call

named_call(name, function); named_call(name, receiver, method)

Register an exact name and a compiler-checked function or bound method. Keep the receiver alive until resume.

cpp
auto call = tracer::launch::named_call("add", &add); if (!tracer::launch::wait_for_resume(call)) return 1;

Command reference

Browse the command appendix for individual commands and examples. See the C++17 branch reference for additional commands and options. Use the first probe for the examples below. Substitute its PID for 12345 and use actual session IDs, probe IDs, addresses, and tokens from your output.

Native REPL startup

bash
clang-tracer-repl --attach 12345 --buffer-events 8192 --cpp-arg "-I."
Option Meaning
--help Print startup usage and exit.
--attach PID, --process FILTER Attach by PID, or find a local process by filter. Choose one.
--endpoint ENDPOINT Use an existing server. Overrides CLANG_TRACER_ENDPOINT. Without either, the REPL manages a private server.
--server PATH, --agent PATH Override the executable and agent for the managed server.
--timeout SEC Default client deadline in seconds. The default is 30, with a maximum of 300.
--buffer-events N, --buffer-bytes N Total retained collection capacity. Defaults are 4096 events and 64 MiB.
--context-event-bytes N, --context-transport-memory-bytes N Managed server's shared event and transport memory budgets.
--cpp-arg ARG Append one local interpreter compiler argument. Repeat for additional arguments. Use separate tokens, e.g. --cpp-arg "-I.".
--extra-arg=ARG, --extra-args FLAGS Append one probe compiler argument or a shell-quoted list to the probe defaults. Repeat as needed.
--startup FILE Read commands and C++ from a local script.
--fail-fast Exit after the first input failure. Useful with redirected scripts or --startup.

Inside the REPL, quote selectors and paths containing spaces. Commands start with %. Other input is evaluated as C++. Use %help probe inject, %help api Event, and Tab completion to look up commands and C++ names.

Native REPL session and discovery commands

Command and example Options and behavior
%server start --agent /opt/tracer/lib64/libclang_tracer_agent.so Start and own a private server. --executable PATH and --agent PATH override the paths. --context-event-bytes N and --context-transport-memory-bytes N override managed transport budgets.
%server connect 127.0.0.1:50051 Switch to an existing endpoint after cleaning up the current connection.
%server status Show current endpoint, readiness, and ownership.
%server stop Stop the owned server and restore its targets.
%processes --filter target List local processes. --filter TEXT narrows the picker candidates.
%attach 12345 --start-time 98765 Attach by PID. Optional --start-time TICKS verifies Linux process identity. Omit PID to use the local picker.
%sessions List known attachments and their probes.
%use s1 Select an attached session for subsequent commands.
%status Show current connection, session, and retained collections.
%detach s1 Detach and restore that session. Omit the ID for the selected session.
%modules --filter libdemo.so --details List application modules from the selected process. --filter TEXT matches a case-sensitive path substring in either listing. --details adds executable mappings, ELF identity, and a mapping token.
%threads List selected target threads, including TIDs, names, and start times.
%symbols --filter add --limit 20 --addresses Browse supported DWARF callables. --filter TEXT matches a substring and --module TEXT narrows module paths. --limit N is a page size, with 0 meaning unbounded. --page TOKEN continues the query. --addresses adds verified live entries. --mapping TOKEN supplies a module mapping snapshot. --address PC --mapping TOKEN looks up a live PC and disables paging.

Native REPL module index commands

See the module index walkthrough for a complete example. Queries and emission work offline once the index exists.

Command and example Options and behavior
%module index --file ./target --output target.sqlite Index a local Linux x86-64 ELF. --file ELF requires no attached process.
%module index --module /path/to/target --mapping TOKEN --output live.sqlite Index an attached module using the REPL's own local Linux server. Both --module PATH and --mapping TOKEN come from %modules --details. Refresh a stale token before retrying.
%module use target.sqlite Select a saved index for subsequent queries, emission, and probe preparation.
%module types --index target.sqlite --filter "demo::*" --limit 10 List named types and known sizes. Accepts the query options below.
%module symbols --index target.sqlite --filter "demo::*" --exported List symbol IDs and selectors. --exported selects dynamic exports. Accepts the query options below.
%module show --symbol "add(int, int)" Print one detailed JSON record. Choose exactly one of --type NAME, --symbol SELECTOR, or --id ID. Add --index INDEX to select an index explicitly.
%module emit --symbol "add(int, int)" --output recovered-add Write declarations.hpp, views.hpp, and manifest.json to a new directory. Repeat --type NAME, --symbol SELECTOR, or --id ID to select entries. Add --index INDEX to select an index explicitly.
Option Meaning
Index --output INDEX Write a new SQLite file. Defaults to <ELF>.tracer.sqlite. Successful indexing selects it for the current REPL.
Index --debug-file FILE Supply matching separate debug information. Without this option, the indexer looks for a verified companion and can read embedded DWARF.
Index --max-entries N, --max-depth N Bound scanned entries and DWARF depth. Omit or pass zero for no limit. Exceeding a budget aborts the build. Ctrl+C cancels REPL indexing.
Query --index INDEX Read this index for the command. Otherwise use the selected index, then module-index.sqlite in the current directory.
Query --filter GLOB Match named types or symbol names, selectors and linkage names with a glob. Quote patterns.
Query --limit N, --page TOKEN Limit a list and continue with the returned next_page token. Zero or omitted limit returns all matches. Keep the same index, filter, and export selection when paging.
Query --format json Return an object with entries and next_page from types or symbols.

Standalone module index CLI

Use clang-tracer-module for shell scripts and offline indexing. It takes local file paths and prints JSON for index metadata and queries.

Command and example Options and behavior
clang-tracer-module --help Show usage.
clang-tracer-module index --file ./target --output target.sqlite Create an index. The REPL's file-mode --output, --debug-file, --max-entries, and --max-depth options apply.
clang-tracer-module info --index target.sqlite Print the indexed ELF identity, debug provenance, and diagnostics.
clang-tracer-module types --index target.sqlite --filter int List types. Supports --filter, --limit, and --page.
clang-tracer-module symbols --index target.sqlite --exported --limit 20 List symbols. Supports --filter, --limit, --page, and --exported.
clang-tracer-module show --index target.sqlite --symbol "add(int, int)" Show one record. Use exactly one of --symbol SELECTOR, --type NAME, or --id ID.
clang-tracer-module emit --index target.sqlite --symbol SYMBOL_ID --output recovered-add Emit headers and manifest. Copy IDs from the query results and repeat --symbol SYMBOL_ID or --type TYPE_ID.

Native REPL probe and bulk trace commands

Command and example Options and behavior
%probe prepare "add(int, int)" --include add.hpp --output prepared Generate a reusable local package. The first --include HEADER supplies the declaration and additional includes supply types. --output NEW_DIR must be new. --compdb PATH selects the compilation database, defaulting to the command's directory. --translation-unit FILE selects an explicit command. --module ELF pins ELF identity. --metadata-only skips adapter files. --no-automatic-members disables automatic pointer-member selection. --follow-depth, --follow-members, --string-bytes and the other followed-member limits are listed with defaults and ranges in Followed-member limits. Accepts extra compiler arguments and --cwd.
%probe prepare "add(int, int)" --module-index target.sqlite --output prepared-add Prepare from an index using the recorded ELF path, or pass --module ELF to verify an explicit path to the same build. Use --id ID to disambiguate a matching selector and --generated DIR to reuse a verified emitted bundle. Accepts --cwd and --metadata-only.
%probe prepare "add(int, int)" --signature "int(int, int)" --module ./target --output prepared-explicit Prepare from a user-supplied function type and ELF. Use --member for an unqualified instance method. Accepts --cwd and --metadata-only.
%probe resolve "add(int, int)" Show resolved signature, ABI and target metadata. Accepts resolution options below.
%probe validate "add(int, int)" --callback hook.cpp Compile and link the local callback without installing it. Accepts resolution options.
%probe inject "add(int, int)" --callback hook.cpp --stack-depth 16 Install or replace the probe. Accepts resolution and deployment options.
%probe entry "add(int, int)" --mapping TOKEN Inspect verified machine-code entry, patch window and control flow. Add --module PATH to disambiguate. For explicit entry use %probe entry --module PATH --elf-address 0x401000 --abi linux-x86-64-sysv --mapping TOKEN. The address is ELF-relative, before ASLR. Both forms accept --cwd.
%probe reload PROBE_ID --callback updated.cpp Compile a new observer and switch the active generation while existing calls finish on their original one. Accepts --cwd.
%probe remove PROBE_ID Restore original code for the probe ID. Accepts --cwd.
%probes List probes in the selected session. Accepts --cwd.
%interceptor load hook.cpp --as observer Read a local callback into a named draft.
%interceptor edit observer Enter multiline source. Finish with .end to save or .cancel to discard.
%interceptor show observer Print the draft source.
%interceptor validate observer --target "add(int, int)" Check a draft against the target selector. Accepts resolution options except --cwd.
%interceptor upload observer --target "add(int, int)" Install a draft. Accepts resolution and deployment options except --cwd.
%trace preview --exact "add(int, int)" --save trace.textproto Report eligibility and capacity before installing anything. Select using repeatable --module GLOB, --include GLOB, --exclude GLOB, and --exact SELECTOR. Require an include or exact rule. Alternatively --manifest FILE loads rules, and --save NEW_FILE writes the manifest.
%trace apply --manifest trace.textproto --callback hook.cpp Install eligible probes in a batch. --callback FILE overrides the default observer. The server attempts to restore newly installed probes on partial failure.
%trace remove batch-1 Restore the probes owned by the returned batch ID, or retry restoration.

For indexed preparation, supply neither headers nor an explicit signature. The search order is --module-index INDEX, then <ELF>.tracer.sqlite when --module ELF is given, then the index selected with %module index or %module use, then module-index.sqlite in the command's working directory. Use --prepared DIR --prepared-mode require when validating and injecting the resulting package.

Resolution and deployment option Meaning
--include HEADER, --compdb PATH Repeat --include for supplemental headers. Use --compdb for the flags used to compile the target.
--translation-unit FILE, --module ELF Select the exact compilation command and narrow ELF resolution respectively.
--compile-option ARG Append one target compilation argument. Repeat in order.
--extra-arg ARG, --extra-args FLAGS Pass one extra argument or a list. Lists can use backtick shell expansion. Probe compiler settings are separate from local C++ interpreter settings.
--cwd DIR Resolve supported relative paths against a per-command working directory.
--prepared DIR, --prepared-mode off|prefer|require Use a local prepared package. The default is prefer when a package is specified or was prepared in this REPL, and off otherwise. off uses live resolution and require fails if the package cannot be used.
--stack-depth N|full, --stack-application-only true|false Deployment only. Request entry stack capture. Zero disables automatic capture. full follows the supported unwind chain. The default frame filter shows application frames.
--print-arguments, --print-result Deployment only. Include automatically captured arguments and result in events. Explicit callback fields remain independently available.

Native REPL memory and C++ commands

Command and example Options and behavior
%memory maps List memory ranges and permissions and obtain a memory snapshot token.
%memory read 0x404000 --mapping TOKEN --type u32 Read from a verified readable mapping. Choose --count BYTES for hex output (up to 65,536 bytes), or --type with u8/u16/u32/u64, i8/i16/i32/i64, f32, or f64 for one little-endian value.
%memory scan 0x404000 --mapping TOKEN --count 64 --pattern "2a ??" --limit 4 Scan a readable range of up to 1 MiB for hex bytes. ? matches a wildcard nibble. --limit N defaults to 64 results and is capped at 1024.
%cpp load analysis.cpp Evaluate a local C++ file in the current interpreter.
%cpp reset Reset C++ declarations, variables and background capture handles. Active tracing sessions stay attached.
%cpp import model.hpp --type app::Order Generate, cache and load record mappings from the header's AST. Repeat --type TYPE to select records. --output FILE writes the generated header.
%cpp generate model.hpp --output mappings.hpp Generate reusable mappings. Repeat --type TYPE to select records. Use --output FILE to save.
%cpp options Print the effective local compiler flags.
%cpp options add "-I/opt/app/include" "-DFEATURE=1" Add flags before first C++ input. Quote flags containing spaces. Backticks can add arguments from shell output.
%cpp options clear Clear custom flags. Reset the interpreter first if it has already evaluated C++ input.
%cpp options compdb build/compile_commands.json --file src/target.cpp Load flags from the selected database and source entry, with same-directory fallback.
%shell "pwd" Run a local shell command and display output.
%complete "tracer." List semantic completions for a C++ prefix without evaluating it.
%type tracer.events_async Show the C++ type or available signatures.
%help api Event Show a command or API topic. %help lists commands and %help api lists API topics.
%quit or %exit Exit, detach sessions owned by this REPL, and stop its private server.

Native REPL capture and recording commands

Command and example Options and behavior
%events --count 2 --as live Print events as they arrive and retain the live collection by default. Accepts stream options.
%collect --count 2 --as sample Retain events with a capture summary. Defaults to collection batch. Accepts stream options.
%record capture.db --sqlite --count 2 Record to a new framed Protobuf file by default. With --sqlite, create or append to SQLite and save available prepared C++ types. Accepts stream options except --as.
%events list sample --limit 10 List indexed summaries. --limit N defaults to 20.
%events show sample --index 1 Print one event and its values by zero-based index.
%events stack sample --index 0 Print one event's full retained stack and capture status.
%events calls sample Pair PRE with POST or EXCEPTION, report durations and identify missing events.
%events stats sample Aggregate call counts, duration buckets, caller edges and loss per probe.
%events clear sample Release the named collection's buffer allocation.
%events open capture.db --as replayed Replay framed Protobuf or SQLite into a new named bounded collection. SQLite can load stored C++ types and mappings.
%events export replayed --format json --output capture.json Write a new JSON export. JSON is the supported export format.
Stream option Meaning
--count N, --timeout SEC Stop after N matching events or at the deadline. Without a count, streams normally run until Ctrl+C. Counted streams default to a 30-second deadline.
--name NAME, --after CURSOR Match an exact selector, linkage name or custom event name and begin strictly after the cursor. Repeat names for an OR filter.
--session ID, --all Use one named session or every session. Omit both to use the selected session.
--probe ID, --phase PRE|POST|EXCEPTION Narrow by probe ID or phase in the client.
--as NAME Name the retained live collection. Valid on %events and %collect.

Ctrl+C cancels active capture and preserves partial results. Trigger new calls from the target terminal while a synchronous capture waits. The native REPL walkthrough explains replay filters, stack attribution, retention and mapping details.

Native server

bash
clang-tracer-server --listen 127.0.0.1:50051 --event-history-limit 8192

Without --listen, the server creates a private Unix endpoint. Use the reported endpoint to connect. Keep TCP tracing endpoints on trusted local interfaces because the native transport uses insecure gRPC. Stop the server with Ctrl+C after detaching.

Option Meaning
--help Show server usage.
--agent LIBRARY Use this injected agent. Lookup then falls back to CLANG_TRACER_AGENT, the installed library, or the adjacent build library.
--listen ENDPOINT Bind a Unix socket (unix:///path/to/socket) or loopback host and port.
--timeout SEC Native operation timeout, default 10 seconds.
--context-durable-dir DIR Keep resumable shared-context journals in this directory.
--event-history-limit N Retain up to N events, default 4096.
--context-history-limit N Retain up to N context events, default 128.
--context-history-bytes N Retained serialized context bytes, default 16 MiB.
--context-event-bytes N Shared event byte budget, default 256 KiB.
--context-transport-memory-bytes N Total shared transport memory budget, default 64 MiB.

Set CLANG_TRACER_AGENT_LOG in the target application's environment to enable per-session agent logs. See callback diagnostics.

Native command-line client

Use --endpoint ENDPOINT to select the server. The default is CLANG_TRACER_ENDPOINT or 127.0.0.1:50051. --help and -h print usage. Direct commands support --format text|protobuf and --output FILE where applicable. Text is the default and output normally goes to stdout. The binary format uses a four-byte little-endian length before each Protobuf message. SQLite output has its own file option.

Command and example Behavior
clang-tracer attach 12345 Attach by PID.
clang-tracer list List sessions and probes.
clang-tracer resolve 12345 "add(int, int)" Resolve a callable. Accepts resolution options below.
clang-tracer validate 12345 "add(int, int)" --callback hook.cpp --level compile Check callback source. --level syntax parses the callback and compile also checks code generation and symbols. Accepts resolution options.
clang-tracer trace 12345 "add(int, int)" --callback hook.cpp --stack 16 Install a callback using DWARF. Accepts resolution and trace options.
clang-tracer trace 12345 --function _Z3addii --return int32 --arg int32 --arg int32 --callback legacy.cpp Trace a raw ELF symbol with an explicit ABI. Use --method NAME for a supported non-static method or --function NAME for a free function. Omit explicit types to resolve the named symbol.
clang-tracer events 12345 --count 2 --timeout 30 Stream events for the attached PID. Use --sqlite capture.db to save while preserving server history.
clang-tracer drain 12345 --sqlite capture.db Commit retained events to SQLite and then acknowledge them. Omit PID for all sessions. Add --listen to keep draining future events.
clang-tracer remove 12345 1 Restore one probe by ID.
clang-tracer detach 12345 Restore all probes and detach the process.
Option Meaning
--include HEADER Repeat for server-side headers.
--compdb FILE_OR_DIR Use a compilation database for the headers. Requires --include.
--module PATH Constrain the image used for resolution.
--debug-max-entries N, --debug-max-depth N Bound DWARF traversal. Zero means unlimited.
--compile-option ARG Append one compiler flag. Repeat to pass more flags.
--callback FILE Read C++ source from the client filesystem.
--return TYPE, --arg TYPE Specify raw ABI types. Arguments are ordered, up to eight. Valid types are bool, int32, int64, uint64, float32, float64, and pointer. Return type can also be void.
--stack N|full Capture entry stacks to the given depth or through the supported unwind chain.
--stack-application-only true|false Filter frames to application code by default.
--callback-print-arguments true|false, --callback-print-result true|false Include automatic argument or result snapshots. Both default to false.
--count N, --after SEQUENCE, --timeout SEC Limit event count, resume strictly after a cursor, or set a deadline. Unary operations default to 30 seconds and streams are open-ended unless a deadline is supplied.
--context-field path[,path...] Select shared-state field paths for text rendering. Repeat or supply a comma-separated list. Omit to show the union of retained fields.

Legacy mode reads a request from a Protobuf text file with --request FILE. Output is framed Protobuf and can be written to --output FILE. Use --timeout SEC to override the 30-second deadline. Supply --count N for watch. The RPC reference lists the request and response types.

bash
printf 'pid: 12345\n' > attach.textproto
clang-tracer --request attach.textproto --output session.pb attach
clang-tracer --request add.textproto --output probe.pb add
clang-tracer --request remove.textproto --output removed.pb remove
clang-tracer --request detach.textproto --output detached.pb detach
clang-tracer --request list.textproto --output sessions.pb list
clang-tracer --request watch.textproto --count 2 --output events.pb watch

Offline probe preparation

bash
clang-tracer-prepare-injectors-native --selector "add(int, int)" \
  --include add.hpp --compdb build/compile_commands.json \
  --translation-unit target.cpp --output prepared

For offline preparation from a saved index, use the same preparer.

bash
clang-tracer-prepare-injectors-native --selector "add(int, int)" \
  --module-index target.sqlite --module ./target --output prepared-indexed
Option Meaning
--help Show usage.
--selector SELECTOR Required exact C++ selector.
--include HEADER Declaration header for source preparation. Repeat for supporting types.
--compdb FILE_OR_DIR Required compilation database for source preparation.
--translation-unit FILE Select an explicit entry. Otherwise preparation tries the first include's recorded command, then an adjacent source.
--output NEW_DIRECTORY Required new output directory.
--module ELF Pin the package to an ELF build.
--signature TYPE, --member Prepare with an explicit function type. Requires --module. Use --member for an unqualified instance method.
--module-index INDEX, --id ID, --generated DIR Prepare from a saved index, optionally selecting the symbol by ID and reusing an emitted bundle. With no explicit index, the CLI tries the module sidecar and then module-index.sqlite.
--metadata-only Skip separate C++ adapter files.
--extra-arg ARG Append one compiler argument. Repeat as needed.

The REPL starts clang-tracer-repl-check internally for syntax checks, completion, reflection, and replay-type validation. The REPL's %complete, %type, %cpp generate, and recording commands manage that protocol.

Build and deployment scripts

bash
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel --toolchain-root /opt/llvm-21 \
  --prefix /opt/clang-tracer --examples --package TGZ
./deploy-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel --destdir "$PWD/stage"
Script and option Meaning
Both scripts --help, -h Print usage.
Both scripts --build-dir DIR, --prefix DIR Select a build directory (default build-rhel) or installation root. Build defaults to /usr/local. Deploy defaults to the configured prefix.
Build --toolchain-root DIR, --llvm-root DIR Choose compiler and LLVM packages together, or only the LLVM/Clang package prefix.
Build --llvm-dir DIR, --clang-dir DIR Locate the respective CMake packages explicitly.
Build --cc FILE, --cxx FILE, --toolchain-file FILE Set native compilers or a CMake toolchain file.
Build --bindir DIR, --libdir DIR Override installed binary and library directories (defaults bin and lib64).
Build --build-type TYPE, --jobs N Select CMake build type (default RelWithDebInfo) and parallel build jobs (default 2).
Build --examples, --with-tests Build runnable example targets or test fixtures. Run tests separately with CTest.
Build --package TGZ|RPM Package the configured install tree. RPM packaging requires rpmbuild.
Build -- CMAKE_ARGS Forward remaining arguments to CMake configuration.
Deploy --destdir DIR Stage installation under a separate filesystem root.

See Build and deploy for resource headers, custom layouts, and verification.

For Python scripting and console commands, see the optional Python reference.

Clang Tracer developer guide

Use the native REPL and its C++ facade to control a session, index modules, and analyze events. A callback runs inside the application, while an event is serialized and owned by the receiving client. Keep pointers, references, stack views, and context state within the lifetime of the callback. Use an event snapshot when the data needs to survive the call or travel to another process.

Layer Responsibilities
Client Select a target, resolve a callable, validate source, install and remove probes, stream or persist events.
Server Verify target identity, read ELF and DWARF, validate the ABI, coordinate injection, retain events and report loss.
Agent Run the JIT-compiled callback in the target and export captured data through a bounded transport.

Start with the indexed C++ API appendix for methods and examples. See the C++17 branch reference for additional APIs. See the user guide for installation and the first callback, and the tutorials for complete workflows.

Native REPL C++ client API

tracer is the installed REPL's tracer_repl::Facade. The built-in session is the current SessionHandle. Read id, pid, and connection from a handle and acquire a fresh one after reconnecting. %help api lists topics and %type shows overloads in the running interpreter.

Facade method Behavior
module_index(source, output={}, options={}), open_module_index(path={}) Build or open an index and select it. See the native module API.
attach(pid), selected_session(), detach(session) Attach and return a handle, get the selected handle, or restore and detach it.
prepare(selector, header_or_headers, output, compdb={}, translation_unit={}) Generate a reusable package. Supply a string, vector, or braced list of headers with the declaring header first. The output directory must be new.
prepare(selector, header_or_headers, compdb, translation_unit, module, output) Pin a package to an ELF image using the explicit-module overload.
inject(session, selector, callback_file) Install a local callback through live resolution and return the probe ID.
inject(session, selector, callback_file, prepared_directory, prepared_mode="require") Install through a package. Modes are off, prefer, and require.
collect(session, count, timeout_seconds=30) Wait and return a bounded Collection.
events(session, count, timeout_seconds=30) Wait and return an iterable EventRange. Check error() and snapshot() after a failed stream.
events_async(session, count=0, timeout_seconds=0) Return an EventRange immediately and receive in the background. Iterating it waits for events. Zero leaves that limit open.
record(path, options={}) Write SQLite with compatible prepared type metadata. Returns RecordResult.
replay(path, query={}) Read framed Protobuf or SQLite offline into a Collection. Loads compatible recorded C++ mappings from SQLite.
batch(name) Fetch a named retained collection.
print(event), print(collection) Render event details or collection summary.

RecordOptions has session, all_sessions, names, phase, probe_id, after_sequence, count, and timeout_seconds. Omit the session to use the selected attachment. An open-ended count is zero. A zero timeout uses the console default for counted recordings. RecordResult reports received, cursor, complete, cancelled, and timed_out. EventQuery has names, phase, pid, session_id, and count. A zero count reads all matches subject to retention.

Event data types

Type and methods Behavior
Collection::size(), at(index), begin(), end() Count retained events, index with bounds checking, or iterate. Fields events, received, evicted, complete, cancelled, and timed_out expose capture state.
EventRange::snapshot(), running(), error(), stop(), begin(), end() Copy the currently retained events without waiting, check the producer or error text, stop it while retaining data, or iterate from the oldest retained event, waiting for later ones until the range finishes or Ctrl+C. A running range reserves the remaining collection storage; once it finishes or is stopped it keeps only the room its retained events use. Release all range copies to release that too.
Event::sequence(), probe_id(), call_id(), phase(), function_name() Read the event cursor, emitting probe, call identity, phase, and name.
Event::has_result(), argument_value(index), result_value() Check return presence or decode a scalar into ScalarValue (bool, signed or unsigned 64-bit integer, or double). Void is present but has no scalar value.
Event::stack() Return an owned std::vector<tracer_repl::StackFrame> in capture order. Empty when the event has no stored frames.
Event::argument_snapshot(index), result_snapshot(), receiver_snapshot(), state_snapshot(index=0) Read owned structured data from an argument, return, method receiver, or context state. A receiver snapshot represents entry fields.
Event::argument_as<T>(index), result_as<T>(), state_as<T>(index=0) Decode a snapshot into an owning C++ value using EventValue::as<T>().
Event::argument(index), result(), describe() Get display strings for an argument, return, or whole event.
EventValue::cpp_type(), matches_record_type(name), data(), is_null() Inspect the captured type, test record identity, inspect the underlying variant, or check for a null value.
EventValue::field(name), fields(), elements(), at(index), size() Access an object member, the object map, the element array, a checked element, or the size of an object, array, or string. Incompatible shapes and missing members raise exceptions.
EventValue::as<T>(), EventRecord<T>, EventCodec<T> Convert to an owning scalar, supported standard container, or user type. Define EventRecord<T>::type_name and fields() with event_member(name, &T::member), or specialize EventCodec<T>::decode(const EventValue&) for custom construction.

Pipe an EventRange or Collection through tracer_repl::take(n), drop(n), first() (optional value), stride(n), enumerate() (zero-based index and value), filter(predicate), take_while(predicate), drop_while(predicate), or transform(function). to_vector() and reverse() materialize a vector. Filtering and projection run in the foreground as you iterate.

cpp
// Install the probe with --print-result before collecting.
using namespace tracer_repl;
auto live = tracer.events_async(session, 4, 30);
// Trigger two calls in the target terminal. Iteration waits until the range finishes.
auto results = live
    | filter([](const Event& e) { return e.phase() == "POST"; })
    | transform([](const Event& e) { return e.result_as<int>(); })
    | to_vector();
live.stop();

Native C++ module index API

Use this API in the native REPL to build an index, inspect ELF and DWARF metadata, or prepare a probe when you have the binary and debug information. The index is local to the REPL. No target attachment is needed until injection. The user guide shows the equivalent %module commands.

Method Behavior
ModuleSource::file(image, debug_file={}) Select a local ELF and, optionally, its matching separate debug file.
tracer.module_index(source, output={}, options={}) Build and select an index. An empty output path uses <ELF>.tracer.sqlite.
tracer.open_module_index(path={}) Open and select a saved index. With an empty path, use the current index or module-index.sqlite in the working directory.
ModuleIndex::build(source, output, options={}), ModuleIndex::open(path) Build or open an index directly from C++. Direct calls leave the REPL's index selection alone.
path(), identity() Read the SQLite path or the indexed ELF path, SHA-256, build ID, debug companion, and diagnostics.
types(query={}), symbols(query={}) List records and return a page of entries and a next_page token. A query has a glob filter, an optional limit (zero means all), and a continuation page. SymbolQuery::exported_only() restricts the list to dynamic exports.
find_type(name), find_symbol(name) Resolve a type by name or a symbol by selector, name, or linkage name. Exact lookup requires a unique match. Use the full selector for overloaded functions.
get_type(id), get_symbol(id) Read a particular entry using an ID from the same index.
emit_headers(selection, output) Write declarations, read-only field views, and a manifest to a new directory. Fill ModuleSelection::symbols and types with IDs.
prepare_probe(symbol_id, module, output, generated={}, metadata_only=false) Create a prepared package for the indexed symbol. Use an empty module to use the recorded ELF path. The output must be new. An optional generated bundle is checked before reuse. metadata_only keeps the package and skips separate adapter files.

ModuleIndexOptions accepts max_entries and max_depth budgets (zero means unlimited) and a cancelled function that can abort indexing. A ModuleSymbol includes its selector, linkage name, parameter type IDs, and ELF address. Use %symbols --addresses for live PCs. A ModuleType includes its kind, optional size and alignment, and known fields with optional byte or bit offsets.

Prepare and trace with the C++ API

Compile the first-probe target and use its hook.cpp. Run these lines in the native REPL from that directory before attaching. Use new output names on subsequent runs.

cpp
auto index = tracer.module_index(tracer_module::ModuleSource::file("./target"), "target-api.sqlite");
tracer_module::SymbolQuery query;
query.filter = "add*";
auto matches = index.symbols(query);
auto add_symbol = index.find_symbol("add(int, int)");
auto int_type = index.find_type("int");
std::cout << add_symbol.selector << ' ' << int_type.size.value_or(0) << '\n';
index.emit_headers({{add_symbol.id}, {}}, "recovered-add-api");
index.prepare_probe(add_symbol.id, {}, "prepared-add-api", "recovered-add-api");

Run ./target in a second terminal and substitute its printed PID. The fourth argument to tracer.inject selects the prepared package. Press Enter in the target terminal while tracer.collect waits.

cpp
auto indexed_target = tracer.attach(12345);
auto indexed_probe = tracer.inject(indexed_target, add_symbol.selector, "hook.cpp", "prepared-add-api");
auto indexed_events = tracer.collect(indexed_target, 2, 30);
tracer.print(indexed_events.at(1));
tracer.detach(indexed_target);

The POST event shows sum=42. For a later REPL, use tracer.open_module_index("target-api.sqlite"). A standalone C++ application can include <tracer/module_index.hpp> and link tracer_module_index to build, query, and prepare from the same index.

Agent callback API

For a typed callback, define one top-level explicit specialization of Interceptor<Signature> with either or both of pre(const Call&) and post(const Call&). Write the original function type as R(Args...), for example int(int, int), or use tracer::ResolvedSignature to reuse the type recovered from DWARF or a prepared package for the selected target. The callback compiler supplies the primary template, checks the specialization against the target, and exposes its argument and result types through Call. For a supported non-static method, the selector identifies the class and method qualifiers. The signature lists the return and explicit parameter types, and call.self() provides the receiver separately.

Hooks can return void or a long long callback value carried in the event. The original function still receives its arguments and returns its own result. Existing plain class Interceptor callbacks remain supported. Raw-symbol callbacks can use the entry-only extern "C" long long trace_callback(const TraceContext&) API.

The tracer compiles callback source with the effective target flags and checks the supported calling convention. The callback runs on the calling application thread. Keep work bounded and avoid retaining borrowed objects or invoking the probed entry recursively.

Method Behavior
Call::context() Get the current typed shared-context facade.
arg<T>(index), argument<T>(index) Decode a raw argument using a supported scalar or pointer type. Uses a checked zero-based index.
argument<Index>() Read the compiler-generated argument type. References and supported record values are borrowed with read-only access.
argument<T>(name, index) Decode and emit an explicitly named argument, then return it.
argument_count(), argument_name(index), argument_value(index) Read argument metadata and the raw TraceValue. Names fall back to arg0, arg1, and so on.
result<T>(), result<>() Read the original result in POST. Supply a type explicitly or use the inferred type on a typed probe. For supported objects and references the result is borrowed. void checks the return tag and produces no value.
result_value() Read the original raw result in POST.
object_address(), self() Read the receiver address or typed const receiver for a supported non-static method. Free and static functions have no receiver.
field(name, value), field(member_expression) Emit a named field from a supported value. The one-argument form uses Clang member-name inference for supported member expressions. Use the explicit form for computed values.
probe_id(), id() Return the probe ID and invocation ID. PRE and POST for the same call share the invocation ID.
print_options() Read the requested automatic argument and result rendering preferences.
capture_stack(depth=16), capture_stack(depth, application_only) Capture and symbolize the entry stack from either hook. The one-argument form uses the probe's filter. A positive depth is required.
stack() Read the invocation's current stack snapshot, including automatic capture when enabled.
log(message, level=tracer::LogLevel::Info) Queue a diagnostic and return whether it was accepted. Levels are Info, Warning, and Error.
TraceContext::log(message, level) Same queue from a legacy callback. Legacy code reads probe_id, call_id, phase, argument_count, arguments, argument_names, object_address, result, and stack directly.

TraceValue has a type tag, signed, unsigned, and real slots, and an optional snapshot. Decode the slot matching the tag. For snapshots, check the status and detail before reading the owned event representation. StackTrace has status, requested and captured depth, count, hidden frame count, filter, detail, and a borrowed frames array. Each frame can carry PC, stack pointer, kind, function, module, module offset, file, line, and application classification.

cpp
template <>
class Interceptor<int(int, int)> {
public:
  void pre(const Call& call) {
    call.field("left", call.argument<0>());
    const auto& stack = call.capture_stack(12);
    call.field("visible_frames", stack.count);
    call.log("entered add");
  }

  long long post(const Call& call) {
    const int sum = call.result();
    call.field("sum", sum);
    return sum;
  }
};

For a reusable specialization and a concrete C++ template target, see Trace a function template instantiation.

Set CLANG_TRACER_AGENT_LOG to an absolute writable log path in the target's environment before launching it. The target owns the private log. Records include PID, probe ID, call ID and phase where applicable. Messages are capped at 192 bytes and delivered on a best-effort basis.

With logging enabled, the agent also writes an operation=hook record for each PRE and POST hook it runs, after the messages logged by that hook. Its outcome is ok, or failed when the hook threw or could not run. Hook records and callback messages share one queue per probe. When it overflows, the agent writes operation=log stage=queue outcome=dropped with the number of lost records.

Shared context API

Declare payloads with state<Scope> or shared_state<Scope>. Declare hook dependencies with State<T> in the interceptor constructor. Shared state follows the engine's guarded access rules, while ordinary state requires synchronization by the callback author. Use the shared context walkthrough for package lineage, propagation and durable recording.

Method Behavior
Context::get<T>(), get<Scope, Payload>() Access a bound typed payload in the current invocation or identify it by scope and payload type.
Context::with<T>(visitor), with<Scope, Payload>(visitor) Invoke a visitor with the selected state under its scoped access rules.
Context::init_scope<Scope>(), init_scope<Scope>(payload) Start a scope, optionally with a typed initial payload.
Context::end_scope<Scope>() End the named scope. Accepted child work can keep leases until completion.
Context::event(name, max_items=100) Publish a named descriptor-backed snapshot. The permitted item cap is 0–4096. Events can be dropped when their transport or descriptor budget is exhausted.
Context::thread_id() Return the current Linux thread ID.
ScopeInit::root_call() Read the root invocation when constructing a payload that accepts const ScopeInit&.
cpp
struct RequestScope {};
struct RequestState : shared_state<RequestScope> {
  int total = 0;
};

template <>
class Interceptor<int(int, int)> {
public:
  Interceptor(State<RequestState>);

  void post(const Call& call) {
    call.context().with<RequestState>([&](RequestState& state) {
      state.total = call.result();
    });
    call.context().event("request.completed");
  }
};

gRPC control API

Generate bindings from tracer.proto and its imported context_transport.proto. The Development install component includes both schema files under share/clang-tracer/proto. The clangtracer.v1.Tracer service exposes the following methods. Requests that act on a process after attach carry its session ID.

RPC Request → response Behavior
Attach AttachRequest → Session Verify and attach a PID. Optionally verify its observed Linux start time.
ResolveProbe ResolveProbeRequest → ProbeSpec Resolve a callable on the server host.
ValidateProbe ValidateProbeRequest → ValidationReport Check syntax or compile a candidate without activation.
AddProbe AddProbeRequest → Probe Install the supplied probe spec.
ReloadProbe ReloadProbeRequest → ReloadProbeResponse Switch the active callback generation.
RemoveProbe RemoveProbeRequest → Probe Restore one probe.
Detach DetachRequest → Session Restore and detach a session.
ListSessions ListSessionsRequest → ListSessionsResponse List attachments and probes. Also used for readiness.
ListModules ListModulesRequest → ListModulesResponse List eligible modules and optionally verified mapping details.
ListMemoryMappings ListMemoryMappingsRequest → ListMemoryMappingsResponse Get memory ranges and a snapshot token.
ReadMemory ReadMemoryRequest → ReadMemoryResponse Copy a verified readable range.
ScanMemory ScanMemoryRequest → ScanMemoryResponse Search a verified range using a byte pattern and mask.
PreviewFunctionEntry PreviewFunctionEntryRequest → PreviewFunctionEntryResponse Verify live entry bytes and report disassembly and patch eligibility.
ListThreads ListThreadsRequest → ListThreadsResponse List attached target threads and identities.
ListSymbols ListSymbolsRequest → ListSymbolsResponse Browse callables, paginate, request verified addresses, or reverse-lookup a PC.
PreviewBulkTrace PreviewBulkTraceRequest → PreviewBulkTraceResponse Preview rules against the live target and retained capacity.
ApplyBulkTrace ApplyBulkTraceRequest → BulkTraceReport Install a batch using an ID and optional observer source.
RemoveBulkTrace RemoveBulkTraceRequest → BulkTraceReport Restore a named batch.
WatchEvents WatchEventsRequest → stream TraceEvent Stream events after a cursor with session, PID, and exact-name filters.
ReadEvents ReadEventsRequest → ReadEventsResponse Read a bounded retained window without consuming it.
AcknowledgeEvents AcknowledgeEventsRequest → AcknowledgeEventsResponse Consume exact sequences from the matching server lifetime after committing storage.

The agent-to-collector ContextTransport.Export RPC is a bidirectional stream of ProducerPacket and CollectorControl. The agent uses it to deliver state descriptors and events, maintain producer identity, and process collector control. Client applications consume these events through Tracer.WatchEvents or retained history.

Build and validate changes

Use a fresh build directory for a different compiler or SDK. Configure and run the native integration tests.

bash
./build-rhel.sh --toolchain-root /opt/llvm-21 --build-dir build-rhel --with-tests
ctest --test-dir build-rhel --output-on-failure

For Python integration and its tests, see the optional Python reference. See validation for detour regressions and benchmark reproduction. To regenerate the REPL grammar, follow the ANTLR walkthrough.

C++17 branch reference

The native REPL on this branch includes the operations below. Use %help COMMAND for the syntax provided by your installed build. Target control and mutation commands require a compatible local Linux server. Use a disposable target for the examples that modify its behavior.

Launch, control, and profile a target

Command and example Options and behavior
%launch ./app --arg sample --env MODE=test --cwd ./work Launch and attach at the startup checkpoint. Repeat --arg VALUE and --env NAME=VALUE. --cwd DIR selects the working directory. --stdin FILE supplies input. --stdout NEW_FILE and --stderr NEW_FILE select new output files. --timeout SEC bounds startup. --preload PATH selects a launch gate library. --supervise enables owned process-tree supervision and --gate-children pauses supported exec descendants.
%children List paused exec descendants of owned gated launches.
%resume 12345, %terminate 12345 Release the startup gate or terminate and reap an owned target. Omit the PID for the selected target.
%call app::scale --arg 6 --arg 1.5 --timeout 5 Invoke a registered scalar function on the paused startup thread. Repeat --arg in signature order.
%call-result --timeout 5 Wait for a previous call that timed out or was interrupted.
%modules --elf /path/to/app Show imports, exports, and sections from the selected mapped ELF. Use %modules --watch --count 5 --timeout 10 to report mapping changes.
%library load /path/to/libdemo.so Load a trusted server-side shared object into the selected target. It stays loaded until the target exits.
%syscalls --count 20 --timeout 5 Trace syscall entry and exit on existing threads.
%faults --count 10 --timeout 5 Observe delivered fault signals via Linux tracefs.
%sample cpu --count 20 --timeout 5 Sample user-space PCs with Linux perf.
%sample allocations --count 20 --timeout 5 Capture allocation requests to glibc malloc, calloc, and realloc via perf uprobes.

For profiling and module watching, --count N bounds the records and --timeout SEC bounds the capture. See launch and call walkthroughs and local sampling.

Inspect and change target memory

Get a fresh mapping token with %memory maps and a thread ID with %threads. Use live addresses for data and watchpoints. The executable patch form uses the ELF-relative address from %probe entry. Substitute actual addresses and IDs in the examples.

Command and example Options and behavior
%memory allocate 4096, %memory free ALLOCATION_ID Allocate up to 1 MiB of zeroed memory owned by this session. Restore patches on an allocation before freeing it.
%memory write ADDRESS --mapping TOKEN --expect "00" --replace "2a" Write up to 256 bytes in a verified private writable mapping. Expected bytes must match and the replacement must have the same length.
%memory patch --module ELF --elf-address ADDRESS --mapping TOKEN --expect "55" --replace "90" Apply a verified same-width instruction patch at the selected entry. Provide bytes and complete instructions appropriate to that entry.
%memory import-hook --module ELF --symbol NAME --original PC --address REPLACEMENT --mapping TOKEN --abi linux-x86-64-sysv Redirect one resolved import slot. Verify the original address and use an ABI-compatible replacement in the main executable.
%memory restore PATCH_ID Restore the original bytes for a write, executable patch, or import hook.
%memory monitor-start --tid TID --address ADDRESS --size 4096 --mapping TOKEN --timeout 5 Monitor the nominated thread's first touch on dedicated pages. --size is the range in bytes. --timeout bounds protection changes.
%memory monitor-stop Restore original protections and print first touches.
%watchpoint --tid TID --address ADDRESS --size 4 --mapping TOKEN --access write --count 4 --timeout 5 Set a hardware watchpoint on a naturally aligned 1, 2, 4, or 8-byte range. --access accepts write or read-write.

An allocation lab starts with %memory allocate 4096. Use the returned address and a fresh token with the one-byte write above. Read the byte with %memory read ADDRESS --mapping TOKEN --type u8 and expect 42. Restore the returned patch ID, read again and expect zero, then free the allocation.

Capture instructions and replay them

The optional Gum backend records instructions on one nominated thread within a verified executable range. Obtain TID, ADDRESS, and TOKEN using %threads, %probe entry, and %memory maps. The target needs an eligible separate control thread.

bash
%instructions start --tid TID --address ADDRESS --size 32 --mapping TOKEN --count 64 --timeout 5
%instructions stop --save instructions.pb
%instructions replay instructions.pb

Trigger the selected function while capture runs, then stop and save. Replay prints the saved capture without a live target. --size BYTES defines the executable window, --count N caps records, and --timeout SEC caps elapsed time. --registers includes general-purpose register snapshots. --callback-library PATH selects a trusted native instruction callback. --memory-address ADDRESS --memory-size BYTES filters scalar memory accesses. --discover records executed call destinations.

Probe options and callback methods

The following opt-ins apply to validation and deployment. Use the same flags when validating and installing.

Option API and behavior
--allow-arg-overrides Call::override_argument(index, value) stages a scalar argument write in PRE.
--allow-result-override Call::override_result(value) stages a scalar return write in POST.
--allow-replacement Call::replace_with(value) or replace_with() supplies a scalar or void result in PRE and skips the automatic original call.
--allow-call-original Call::call_original<T>() invokes the original from PRE with its entry arguments. Repeat calls return the first result.
--trace-exceptions Publish EXCEPTION events from the original call. Capture them with %events --phase EXCEPTION. The exception still propagates to the caller.
--reclaimable Declare that the observer leaves no escaping JIT addresses or thread-local storage so it can be reclaimed after retirement. Shared-context work is excluded from this contract.
%probe reload PROBE_ID --callback hook.cpp --watch --count 2 --timeout 20 Watch the callback file for changes and reload valid generations. Use --count and --timeout to bound the watch.

See the scalar override tutorial for the target marker, supported scalar types, and local control requirements.

Additional client and callback APIs

A captured native REPL Event::stack() returns an owned vector of frames, including each PC, stack pointer, kind, module, module offset, function, file, line, and application-frame classification.

cpp
for (const auto& frame : tracer.batch("fullstack").at(0).stack())
  std::cout << frame.function << ' ' << frame.file << ':' << frame.line << '\n';

Build and deploy on RHEL-compatible Linux

The native backend requires Linux x86-64, C++20 and matching LLVM/Clang 21 or 22 development libraries. The scripts have been verified on Rocky Linux 9.8 with LLVM/Clang 21.1.8. Red Hat Enterprise Linux itself has not been tested.

Dependencies

Install dependencies using your organization's approved package repositories. Typical RHEL-compatible package names are:

sh
sudo dnf install cmake ninja-build gcc-c++ clang clang-devel clang-libs llvm-devel \
  protobuf-compiler protobuf-devel grpc-devel grpc-plugins sqlite-devel

Repository availability and LLVM versions vary. Confirm the selected packages provide LLVM/Clang 21 or 22; an older distribution default is insufficient. rpm-build is additionally needed for RPM packaging. Neither script installs packages, changes repositories, modifies tracing policy, or creates services.

Select the compiler and LLVM installation

A distribution installation with split CMake package directories can use:

sh
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel \
  --cc /usr/bin/clang --cxx /usr/bin/clang++ \
  --llvm-dir /usr/lib64/llvm21/lib64/cmake/llvm \
  --clang-dir /usr/lib64/cmake/clang \
  --prefix /opt/clang-tracer --jobs 2 --examples

For a self-contained custom LLVM installation:

sh
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-custom \
  --toolchain-root /opt/llvm-21 \
  --prefix /opt/clang-tracer --bindir tools --libdir runtime/lib64 \
  -- -DCMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR=sdk/include

Use the real additional CMake options you need after --; for example:

sh
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-sdk --toolchain-root /opt/llvm-21 \
  --prefix /opt/clang-tracer \
  -- -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH='/opt/grpc;/opt/protobuf' \
     '-DTRACER_JIT_FLAGS=--gcc-toolchain=/opt/gcc-14;--sysroot=/opt/native-sdk'

--toolchain-root selects PREFIX/bin/clang, PREFIX/bin/clang++ (unless CC/CXX or explicit compiler options select others), and LLVM/Clang CMake packages under the prefix. --llvm-root selects only the library packages; --cc and --cxx independently select the build compilers. Explicit --llvm-dir and --clang-dir handle distributions that split those packages across prefixes. An unavailable LLVM root fails configuration rather than selecting system LLVM.

Alternatively, pass --toolchain-file /opt/sdk/native-toolchain.cmake. Standard CC/CXX, CMAKE_C_COMPILER, CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER, CMAKE_SYSROOT, compiler flags and CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH remain supported. Use a fresh build directory when changing compiler or SDK. This supports native Linux x86-64 SDK configurations; cross-compiling the embedded LLVM toolchain is not covered by these scripts.

The selected LLVM package's Clang driver discovers its builtin header directory and is checked for the matching LLVM major. Override discovery with -DTRACER_CLANG_DRIVER=/opt/llvm-21/bin/clang, or explicitly set -DTRACER_CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR=/opt/llvm-21/lib/clang/21. That directory must contain include/stddef.h; an explicit resource override must match the linked Clang version.

The embedded callback compiler is independent of the compiler that built the project. Set TRACER_JIT_FLAGS to a CMake semicolon-separated list of compiler arguments when callbacks need a custom sysroot, GCC installation, include paths, or -stdlib=libc++. These defaults apply to callback JIT compilation, callback syntax checks and optional target-header parsing. Per-request compilation database options follow those defaults for target-header parsing. Supply the corresponding build compiler flags separately, for example -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=--gcc-toolchain=/opt/gcc-14. Use absolute SDK/include paths: the target's working directory may differ from the build directory.

Keep the target and callback ABI compatible, including standard-library versions when exchanging library types. Linking the tracer against LLVM/Clang does not bundle a C++ SDK or alter the target's loaded standard library.

Installation layout

sh
./deploy-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel

The install tree contains:

CMake variable Default in build-rhel.sh Contents
CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX /usr/local Install root
CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR bin clang-tracer, clang-tracer-server
CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR lib64 libclang_tracer_agent.so
CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR include Public tracer/ headers
CMAKE_INSTALL_DATADIR share Protocol schema, example sources, Clang builtin headers
CMAKE_INSTALL_DOCDIR share/doc/clang_tracer README, Markdown and HTML guides, documentation launcher, and licenses

--prefix, --bindir and --libdir configure the common choices in the build script. Pass other GNUInstallDirs variables after --, for example -DCMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR=sdk/include -DCMAKE_INSTALL_DATADIR=assets/share. Relative directories resolve under the prefix. CMake also accepts absolute directories; configure their final locations and prefix before building. For layouts mixing absolute and relative directories, do not override the prefix after configuration or move the installation.

Stage a package tree without touching the live filesystem:

sh
./deploy-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel --destdir "$PWD/stage"

With prefix /opt/clang-tracer, files appear under stage/opt/clang-tracer. DESTDIR is a staging root, not a runtime path. For layouts using relative directories, --prefix /another/prefix overrides the install prefix and the complete installed prefix can be moved together. Do not independently move its binaries, agent and resource headers.

The server finds the agent relative to its executable, including when launched through PATH from another directory. --agent /path/to/library.so overrides that lookup; CLANG_TRACER_AGENT is the next priority. A build-tree server also finds an adjacent agent library.

Matching Clang builtin headers are installed by default and found relative to the executable or injected agent. No build-tree resource directory is needed after installation. Disable copying with -DTRACER_BUNDLE_CLANG_HEADERS=OFF only if a compatible resource directory will remain available on the target host. CLANG_TRACER_CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR=/absolute/resource/directory overrides resource lookup in the process doing compilation. For injected callbacks, set it in the target's environment before starting the target; setting it only on the tracing server does not change an existing target's environment.

The injected agent requires PIC static gRPC, Protobuf and their transport dependencies so they can be isolated from copies already loaded by the target. Supply a static gRPC CMake package through CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH and set -DProtobuf_USE_STATIC_LIBS=ON; the GCC 8.5 recipe in gcc85-compatibility.md builds matching archives. The agent build rejects extra exports and shared transport dependencies. Shared LLVM, Clang and other remaining system dependencies must be available on the deployment host. The install adds a relative agent-library search path and CMake's external link paths; it does not copy dependency DSOs. For nonstandard dependency locations, configure their deployment locations using CMAKE_INSTALL_RPATH or arrange the loader environment on the host, including in the target process for the injected agent. Keep deployment ABI versions compatible with the build host.

Archives and RPMs

sh
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel --prefix /opt/clang-tracer \
  --llvm-dir /usr/lib64/llvm21/lib64/cmake/llvm \
  --clang-dir /usr/lib64/cmake/clang --package TGZ
./build-rhel.sh --build-dir build-rhel --prefix /opt/clang-tracer \
  --llvm-dir /usr/lib64/llvm21/lib64/cmake/llvm \
  --clang-dir /usr/lib64/cmake/clang --package RPM

Packages are placed under build-rhel/packages/. TGZ archives contain a common top-level directory. Both formats preserve the configured installation prefix. RPM installation is a separate administrator action; review the generated package and its dependency list before installing it on a host. Neither format bundles dependency DSOs. --with-tests builds integration fixtures but never runs them; ordinary builds omit those fixtures and example targets unless --examples is requested.

Start the installed runtime with your selected paths:

sh
/opt/clang-tracer/bin/clang-tracer-server \
  --listen unix:///tmp/my-private-directory/control.sock
CLANG_TRACER_ENDPOINT=unix:///tmp/my-private-directory/control.sock \
  /opt/clang-tracer/bin/clang-tracer list

Create that private directory first with mode 0700. Attachment still requires the host's usual process tracing permissions; deployment does not change them.

Verification

On Rocky Linux 9.8 with LLVM/Clang 21.1.8, verification covered a distribution build and a separate build using a native CMake toolchain file, compiler wrappers around the same Clang installation, an explicit LLVM root and custom callback compiler flags. This verifies path selection, rather than a second LLVM version.

The custom build installed into tools, runtime/lib64, sdk/include and assets/share beneath a staged prefix. After overriding that prefix at install time and moving the complete tree again, the server launched through PATH from another directory and found its agent automatically. With the private build-time resource copy temporarily unavailable, the installed agent compiled a callback requiring both builtin headers and the configured JIT macro. Public CLI tracing recorded 12 PRE and 12 POST events, 60 callback stack frames in each phase, zero reported agent/server losses and zero target failures; normal target calls continued after detach. Optional callback value printing remained off and application-only stack filtering remained on.

Both --package TGZ and --package RPM produced packages retaining the selected prefix. Extracted copies of each package started and answered the list RPC with automatic agent discovery. Missing LLVM roots and missing Clang resource headers were rejected during configuration. No package was installed into the live operating system, and the integration suite was not run.

GCC 8.5 SDK compatibility build

This recipe builds clang-tracer against an explicitly supplied SDK directory. Clang provides the C++20 compiler while the target remains compatible with the SDK's glibc 2.23 and libstdc++ 8.5 runtime. It installs all generated dependencies and the application into a scratch directory; it does not use sudo or install into /usr/local.

Validation and measured overhead are recorded in gcc85-runtime-results.md.

Build

Run the script on the Linux build host with the SDK installed and an absolute, writable scratch path:

sh
scripts/gcc85-build.sh /path/to/toolchain /var/tmp/clang-tracer-gcc85 3
# Optional explicit runtime paths:
scripts/gcc85-build.sh /path/to/toolchain /var/tmp/clang-tracer-custom 3 \
  --sysroot /path/to/sysroot --dynamic-loader /path/to/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2
# Optional only for filesystem or mapping changes:
scripts/gcc85-build.sh /path/to/toolchain /var/tmp/clang-tracer-overlay 3 \
  --overlay-tests

The first argument is the absolute SDK path; the second is the absolute scratch path. The third argument is optional and defaults to three jobs. CMake runs from the build host, not the SDK; set TRACER_CMAKE if it is not available under the name cmake. The script selects Ninja when ninja is installed and otherwise uses the host make generator. The SDK path has no hardcoded or environment default. Direct CMake users must pass -DTRACER_SDK_ROOT=/path/to/toolchain alongside the toolchain file; compiler-check subprojects inherit that selection. --sysroot overrides the SDK-layout default for dependency compilation, SQLite, the tracer and embedded JIT flags. --dynamic-loader overrides the executable interpreter for dependency tools and tracer binaries. The loader defaults to lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 beneath the selected sysroot. Both effective paths, the selected host CTest path, and the OverlayFS test mode are recorded in build-environment.txt.

Direct CMake builds accept -DCMAKE_SYSROOT=/path/to/sysroot and -DTRACER_DYNAMIC_LOADER=/path/to/loader. Use a fresh scratch/build directory when changing SDK, sysroot or loader so cached compiler/linker settings cannot silently retain the previous profile.

Binaries and debug files are fixed for each tracing session. Rebuilding or replacing one requires a new session. Module lookup uses canonical mapped paths and ELF load offsets/ranges, without comparing filesystem device/inode numbers or polling binary timestamps. OverlayFS builds do not require a bind-mounted filesystem to satisfy file identity checks.

The script preserves the scratch tree and refuses to replace an existing gRPC checkout if it does not match the pin. It rejects dirty root and recursive submodule sources, allowing only its exact gRPC CPU fallback and protobuf RPATH patches and the pinned zlib CMake configuration's exact zconf.h to zconf.h.included rename. The gRPC patch keeps the CPU fallback quiet when sched_getcpu() returns ENOSYS. Its dependency pins are gRPC tag v1.46.7 at 02384e39185f109bd299eb8482306229967dc970, with recursive shallow submodules (including protobuf 3.19.5), and SQLite 3.34.1 from the official SQLite archive. It records the checked-out gRPC/submodule revisions in dependency-revisions.txt, SQLite's downloaded archive checksum and origin in sqlite3-checksum.txt, the chosen host build tools and inputs in build-environment.txt, and command output under logs/. The official SQLite archive is checked against its pinned SHA-256; SQLITE_EXPECTED_SHA256 can explicitly override that expected value.

The script uses SDK clang/clang++, builds gRPC and SQLite as C++17/PIC Release dependencies, enables only the gRPC C++ plugin, and disables their tests. It patches protobuf's bundled install-RPATH declarations idempotently so the installed executables retain the configured dependency and SDK runtime paths. The SDK already provides LLVM and Clang under lib.llvm; the recipe does not rebuild them. It checks protoc --version before configuring the application with cmake/toolchains/gcc85-sdk.cmake, RelWithDebInfo, and BUILD_TESTING=ON. The application is installed under <scratch>/install.

gRPC, protobuf and gRPC's bundled dependencies are built as static PIC archives. Use a fresh scratch directory when switching from the earlier shared-dependency recipe. The injected agent localizes their symbols with a linker version script and exports only tracer_agent_start, tracer_agent_stop, tracer_agent_validate and tracer_context_pthread_create_detour. Callback JIT helpers are registered by address directly in each interpreter, without relying on ELF exports or LLVM's process-wide symbol registry. This prevents the application's protobuf/gRPC definitions from replacing the agent's copies and prevents the agent from exporting replacements into the application. Shared LLVM/Clang and the target's C/C++ runtime remain dependencies. A build-time audit, also registered as agent_symbol_isolation in CTest, rejects extra exports or shared transport dependencies. grpc_agent_dependency_collision attaches and traces a target exporting deliberately incompatible protobuf/gRPC definitions; grpc_agent_shared_dependency_collision also exercises shared-state gRPC delivery and pthread propagation in that target. These checks do not establish safe recovery from an arbitrary abort inside a loaded library.

Tests

The build script runs the normal CTest suite after building the application and before installing it. A test failure stops the script before installation. It uses the host CTest executable beside the selected host CMake when available, otherwise the host ctest found before adding the SDK to PATH. Test output is saved to <scratch>/logs/tracer-tests.log.

To rerun the normal suite against an existing build:

sh
ctest --test-dir /var/tmp/clang-tracer-gcc85/build/clang-tracer --output-on-failure

OverlayFS tests remain opt-in and should be used only when filesystem or process-mapping code changes, such as mapped-path resolution, /proc mapping parsing, or ELF load-segment mapping. Pass --overlay-tests to run them after the normal suite and before installation:

sh
scripts/gcc85-build.sh /path/to/toolchain \
  /var/tmp/clang-tracer-gcc85-overlay 3 --overlay-tests

The OverlayFS runner uses a private test namespace and leaves the host build tree unchanged. It requires user/mount namespaces and OverlayFS support; ordinary builds and tracer use do not require these test facilities. Its output is saved to <scratch>/logs/tracer-overlay-tests.log. The script uses the selected host CTest directory for this run and stops before installation if either suite fails.

Compatibility details

The SDK compiler can parse C++20 while the target standard library predates parts of that library. include/tracer/compat.hpp selects standard std::span when available and otherwise provides a dynamic-extent view, plus compatibility helpers for byte views, bit_cast, countr_zero, construct_at, string prefix/suffix/membership checks, bit predicates, sequence erasure, and remove_cvref_t. Define TRACER_FORCE_COMPAT_LIBRARY=1 when compiling compatibility checks to exercise the project fallback even with a newer host library.

Runtime paths include both lib and lib64 in the scratch dependency prefix, the SDK's x86_64-1a-linux-gnu/lib64, and its sysroot lib64. Executables use the SDK loader explicitly. This keeps the binaries and shared libraries tied to the intended older runtime instead of depending on whichever loader happens to be first on the host.

The loader validates actual ELF SONAMEs and mapped paths, including older libc-2.23.so and libpthread-2.23.so filenames. For an application without libdl loaded, bootstrap uses the matching libc's private loader entry points. Runtime calls use the canonical mapped module path and load bias, with live entry-instruction checks for the loader and pthread entry points. GNU build IDs and binary rebuild polling are not required. A second shared probe can normalize only this session's verified existing pthread detour.

The SDK's libc process-vm wrappers are stubs; native memory reads/writes use the supported x86-64 kernel syscalls directly. The running kernel must still support the tracer's existing ptrace and process-vm operations; the SDK name does not establish compatibility with a Linux 2.6.32 kernel.

The private standard-library image uses the SDK's exact static archives, retains only available helper roots, and also supplies GCC 8's out-of-line character allocator constructors. Sealed gthread markers are bound privately; an attempted actual key creation traps. The runtime checks allow either the verified libc forwarding mutex stubs or the separate pthread implementation. They continue rejecting application interposition. Native state/exception RTTI remains enabled; only the LLVM memory-manager/importer translation units match the SDK LLVM build's disabled RTTI.

Lifecycle fingerprints use version 2: module-local LLVM attribute-group numbers are normalized while actual function, dependency and call attributes remain part of the fingerprint. Unrelated template instantiations can no longer split an otherwise identical scope generation. Quoted #number data and semantic attribute changes still distinguish generations.

Embedded compilation disables automatic host C++ include discovery and uses the native compiler's recorded include roots. This applies to private owner activation, SDK agent callbacks, and analysis-test compilation; a newer host GCC installation cannot supply optional headers missing from the SDK library. For example, GCC 11's <span> must not be combined with GCC 8's type_traits.

ELF validation checks complete file-backed PT_LOAD ranges by canonical path, permissions and file offsets, including segments that begin inside a merged mapping or span several mappings. Distinct complete load biases remain ambiguous and are rejected. Missing mappings and incomplete segment coverage remain errors. Native stack caches are reset for a new session after prior callbacks drain; adding probes within the same session reuses those caches.

The controller must map the same runtime ELF files as its target. Use the SDK-built controller with the original SDK-runtime target. The installed modern agent cannot run in that older runtime, and loading an SDK agent's old libdl/pthread into a modern libc process is not a valid control. Benchmarks therefore compare the same GCC 8.5 workload and shared library under each build's matching runtime. Their differences include compiler/library and dependency effects; they do not isolate just the compatibility helpers.

Legacy libc lacks the newer dedicated main-call wrapper. Busy-main admission therefore requires the exact ELF main function and a direct startup chain. If that leader is blocked in another syscall, an eligible existing worker can host injection. A sleeping worker retains the original interrupted-sleep policy; a directly started pthread worker in userspace must have bounded application CFI ending at exact start_thread in the mapped SDK libpthread.so.0, then exact __clone in the mapped libc. No arbitrary blocked syscall becomes an injection host. Worker TLS and the separation between the process PID and host TID are validated. Unsupported all-blocked and external job-stop cases report FAILED_PRECONDITION after safe release, without false shutdown cleanup errors. A fully stripped busy executable without that proof is rejected; idle attach remains available. The legacy stripped-admission regression checks that rejection and subsequent progress, while the modern-runtime regression still checks successful stripped busy-main admission.

Entry instruction relocation retains its existing restrictions. The separate signature Interceptor implementation adds ABI-proven object forwarding; the SDK profile alone does not establish GCC 8 by-value class ABI evidence or arbitrary RIP-relative entry relocation. Positive test fixtures use stack locals before global accesses so compiler PIE defaults do not turn them into tests of that separate entry-relocation limitation.

GCC 8.5 runtime compatibility validation — 2026-11-02

The compatibility implementation is in branch c++17, based on e9856259e2ecb538e098f99c30c50c1a88320afb. Its managed worktree is /Users/husam/.codex/worktrees/gcc85-runtime/clang-tracer. The primary checkout, installed baseline, and original application binaries were preserved.

The current session contract treats binaries/debug files as fixed until detach. A rebuild requires a new session. Canonical mapped paths and ELF load ranges replace device/inode equality and live binary-rebuild policing; the historical bind-mount workaround below is superseded by this policy.

Build and application validation

On linux-dev, the full native build uses SDK /opt/toolchain/x86_64-2.6.32-v4.0.137: Clang 21.1.8, the GCC 8.5 standard library and glibc 2.23. LLVM/Clang stay inside the agent and use the SDK's prebuilt libraries. The tracer remains C++20 internally; this does not require recompiling the C++17 target. gRPC 1.46.7 and its bundled dependencies, protobuf 3.19.5, and SQLite 3.34.1 were built against this runtime.

The remote source, build and install directories are respectively /tmp/tracer-gcc85-build-20261102/source, sdk-build, and install. The installed executable is install/bin/clang-tracer-server, with the agent and sealed standard-library image under install/lib64/. These binaries retain absolute scratch dependency and SDK runtime paths; this install is not a relocatable distribution.

Validation Result

macOS modern-library portable and Clang-analysis suite 6/6 passed, 37.44 seconds

Same application, installed SDK server/agent Attach and all three supported signatures passed
