The default channel uses the existing service's local insecure transport. Programmatic clients can supply a preconfigured gRPC channel, including a secure channel when connecting through a TLS endpoint. The supplied channel remains owned by its caller.

Index a module and prepare a probe without application headers

Use the native Clang Tracer tools on PATH with the Python package. Building and querying an index works offline. Use a matching debug file when the ELF has separate DWARF.

python
from clang_tracer import ModuleIndex, ModuleSource

index = ModuleIndex.build(ModuleSource.file("./libdemo.so"), "demo.sqlite")
packet = index.find_type("demo::Packet")
score = index.find_symbol("demo::score(demo::Packet const&)")
for entry in index.symbols(filter="demo::*", exported_only=True).entries:
    print(entry.id, entry.selector)

index.emit_headers(symbols=[score.id], output="recovered")
prepared = index.prepare_probe(score.id, output="prepared-score", generated="recovered")

Use ModuleIndex.open("demo.sqlite") to reuse an index. types() and symbols() return typed pages. Set limit and pass next_page as page to retrieve another page. get_type(id) and get_symbol(id) resolve IDs within that index. With no output argument, build() creates the <ELF>.tracer.sqlite sidecar. With no module argument, prepare_probe() uses the ELF path stored in the index and verifies its identity. Pass the resulting directory as prepared=prepared to client.validate_probe() or client.inject() on the attached session. The client sends the package contents to the server.

Programmatic tracing

The repository's examples/python/README.md describes runnable programs for attachment, probes, live streams, binary recordings, and server lifecycle, including commands for the native example target.

python
from pathlib import Path
from clang_tracer import Client

with Client("127.0.0.1:50051") as tracer:
    session = tracer.attach(12345)
    probe = tracer.inject(
        session.id,
        "Calculator::add(int, int)",
        Path("interceptor.cpp").read_text(),
        stack_depth=24,
        print_arguments=True,
        print_result=True,
    )
    try:
        for event in tracer.collect_traces(20, session_ids=[session.id], timeout=10):
            print(event.sequence, event.phase, event.call_id, event.stack)
    finally:
        tracer.remove_probe(session.id, probe.id)
        tracer.detach(session.id)

inject() resolves the C++ selector on the server using DWARF, then submits the resulting ProbeSpec with the interceptor source. It requires the additive ResolveProbe RPC introduced with this client. Rebuild/reinstall the native server from this revision before using it; an older server returns gRPC UNIMPLEMENTED. Existing RPCs remain compatible with older servers.

Injecting a target already hooked in the same session replaces that probe with a new ID. Compilation failure leaves the existing hook active. A successful replacement restores and drains the old hook before installing the new one, so there is a brief interval without tracing. The existing 32 retained-probe limit also counts replaced versions. Rebuild the server and agent together for this behavior; an already loaded older agent requires restarting the target.

The console decodes shared-state payloads using each event's bundled schema and shows field values, including strings, nested records, and containers, beneath the payload summary. Invalid payloads produce a diagnostic, and large values are visibly truncated. Pointer arguments still display their captured address.

Callback source is transmitted by value. Optional include_headers, compilation_database and callback_package_path refer to paths on the server host. Package location is optional; pass it when the source belongs to a retained shared-context package. Omitting it follows the native service's isolated source-lineage behavior. The client never assumes a local callback path exists remotely.

compile_options is an ordered list of compiler arguments for resolving and compiling the callback. Pass it to either resolve_probe() or inject(); inject() carries the same options through resolution and AddProbe, and add_probe() preserves options already stored in the ProbeSpec. Include directories and any header/compilation-database paths are interpreted on the server host. For example, use compile_options=["-std=c++17", "-I/opt/app/include"] when the target headers live under /opt/app/include on that host. Supported options cover include paths (-I, -isystem, -iquote, -include), defines and undefines (-D, -U), language standard (-std=), common warning, optimization and debug flags. A compilation database can also supply its matching --sysroot and --gcc-toolchain settings; target triples are checked against the engine. Unsupported compiler flags are rejected before preflight or installation. Forced -include headers are processed in source order during preparation; preflight does not execute their global initializers. Standard-library types such as std::string use the real target headers, and their ABI macros (including _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI) must match the target build. For example, a std::string callback validated against a target built with the new libstdc++ ABI must keep _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1. Object arguments and by-value results are exposed as borrowed references during the callback; a returned object is available only during POST.

Use validate_probe() to check callback source without installing a probe:

python
report = tracer.validate_probe(
    session.id,
    "Calculator::add(int, int)",
    Path("interceptor.cpp").read_text(),
    compile_options=["-std=c++17", "-I/opt/app/include"],
    level="compile",
)
if not report.success:
    for diagnostic in report.diagnostics:
        print(diagnostic.stage, diagnostic.file, diagnostic.line,
              diagnostic.column, diagnostic.message)

level="syntax" checks parsing and reports source diagnostics. The default, level="compile", also generates and checks the complete callback wrapper and its method bindings. Validation does not install or execute callbacks and does not run callback global initializers. The report includes success, diagnostics with severity, stage and source location, and the ordered compiler options supplied for the callback. The console exposes the same operation as probe validate SESSION SELECTOR --callback FILE --level compile; add repeated --compile-option ARG flags for ordered compiler arguments. Validation requires the server's additive ValidateProbe RPC.

resolve_probe(session_id, selector, ...) returns the complete inferred spec without installing it. add_probe(session_id, spec) accepts a generated clang_tracer.messages.ProbeSpec, preserving access to every advanced field and the explicit low-level ABI mode. list_sessions(), remove_probe() and detach() return generated messages too. The generated stubs and all context transport messages are available under clang_tracer.proto; ContextTransport is the native producer/collector protocol, rather than an additional public tracing control API.

Unary RPCs default to a 30-second deadline, configured with Client(timeout=...). Errors retain their original grpc.RpcError status and details. The client performs no implicit control retries because operations can mutate targets.

Discover functions and methods

For an attached session_id, list callable selectors on the tracing host:

python
with Client(endpoint) as tracer:
    page = tracer.list_symbols(session_id, query="Calculator", page_size=20)
    for symbol in page.symbols:
        print(symbol.selector, symbol.linkage_symbol, symbol.module_path)
    if page.next_page_token:
        following = tracer.list_symbols(
            session_id,
            query="Calculator",
            page_size=20,
            page_token=page.next_page_token,
        )

Returned selectors can be passed to resolve_probe() or inject(). Discovery reads mapped application ELF/DWARF images on the server; it requires no target source files on the client. Functions without supported debug signatures are omitted. Listing a function does not bypass probe admission checks.

query matches a case-sensitive substring of the C++ selector or linkage name; module matches a substring of the module path. Listing returns all matches by default (page_size=None or 0). A positive page_size opts into pagination; the server imposes no page-size ceiling or discovery work budget. Keep the same filters and page size when continuing with next_page_token. Tokens are tied to the attached session and mapped images; restart the query if the process or its modules change. This operation requires a server supporting the ListSymbols RPC.

tracer.list_modules(session_id) and console modules list the current mapped application image paths eligible for discovery. By default, probe resolution reads DWARF only in images whose ELF symbol tables list the requested symbol; unrelated images are not traversed. module="/mapped/image" (console --module /mapped/image) explicitly selects an exact absolute path, or use a path substring. Explicit selection also permits DWARF lookup without an ELF symbol-table match. The injected agent revalidates only the selected image.

Debug traversal is unlimited by default. resolve_probe() and inject() accept debug_max_entries and debug_max_depth; zero means unlimited. The console accepts --debug-max-entries N and --debug-max-depth N on probe resolve and probe inject. If an opted-in limit is reached, increase it or pass zero; the server returns RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with the relevant option name.

Receiving and recording traces

python
with Client() as tracer:
    with tracer.watch_events([session_id], after_sequence=last_sequence) as stream:
        for event in stream:
            consume(event)
            last_sequence = stream.after_sequence

Live streams have no deadline unless timeout is supplied. Call stream.close() from another thread to cancel a blocked read, or leave its context manager. Client.close() cancels streams on its owned channel. Empty session filters subscribe to every session; pid optionally filters by process. Every event retains stack frames, shared-context schema/payload bytes, drop counters and PRE/POST correlation fields.

The optional names filter matches emitted event names and full C++ function signatures. For example:

python
with Client(endpoint) as tracer:
    with tracer.watch_events(
        session_ids=[session_id],
        names=["snapshot", "Calculator::multiply(int, int) const"],
        timeout=10,
    ) as stream:
        for event in stream:
            print(event.function_name, event.context.event.name)

Names match exactly, including case, spaces and signature qualifiers. A match against either name is sufficient; session and PID filters must also match. The displayed function_name normally comes from the resolved C++ signature; when that signature exceeds 4096 UTF-8 bytes, the server uses its linkage symbol. Omit names to receive all names. collect_traces() and record_traces() accept the same option and count matching events. Name filtering requires an updated server; the client reports an error if a server returns events outside the requested names. Events retain their global sequence numbers, so filtered results can have expected sequence gaps.

The server's history is bounded. A stale cursor produces OUT_OF_RANGE; the client does not silently reset it or reconnect. Watch the event drop counters and per-probe sequence gaps when assessing completeness. Stream deadlines also raise their gRPC error, including during collection.

collect_traces(count, ..., timeout=30) retains at most count messages in a list. For larger recordings use:

python
with Client() as tracer:
    written = tracer.record_traces(
        "capture.pb",
        100_000,
        session_ids=[session_id],
        timeout=120,
    )

Recordings contain repeated four-byte unsigned little-endian lengths followed by serialized TraceEvent bytes. Recording creates the file exclusively and streams directly to disk. On interruption or RPC failure it preserves completed records in the partial file and cancels the subscription. The exception still propagates; partial data is not reported as a successful complete recording.

Launch, status and shutdown

Both the API and console can launch and own a local native server:

python
with Client() as tracer:
    tracer.start_server()
    print(tracer.status())
    # Attach processes, install probes, and receive events here.
    tracer.shutdown_server(timeout=30)

Set context_event_bytes=25165824 and context_transport_memory_bytes=234881024 in start_server() for 24 MiB shared events. The console equivalent is server start --context-event-bytes 25165824 --context-transport-memory-bytes 234881024.

ServerProcess is also exported for standalone process management. Startup checks that the endpoint is unused, launches without a shell, and waits for a successful ListSessions RPC. Startup output is captured for failure diagnostics. status() distinguishes service readiness from ownership of a child process. Owned channels keep their connection state separate and use bounded reconnect delays, so failed status checks before launch cannot leave startup waiting on another client's connection backoff. Readiness waits for the RPC to succeed; printing a listening address alone does not establish readiness. A startup timeout includes the last readiness RPC status. Caller-supplied channels retain their own transport settings, and mutating RPCs are not automatically replayed. The startup timeout covers both readiness phases; graceful target restoration after a failure can take additional time. If the caller's channel cannot become ready after launch, the client retains ownership so it can still shut down the managed server.

Shutdown sends SIGTERM to the owned child and waits for the native server to detach sessions and restore probes. A nonzero exit is an error. If graceful shutdown times out, ownership remains available for a later retry; the manager does not force-kill a server while it may still be restoring targets. Closing the client or exiting the console also shuts down its managed server. The child has its own process session, so terminal Ctrl-C only interrupts the console. Shutdown retries wait for the same cleanup without sending another signal.

An independently running or remote server can be queried with status(), but cannot be terminated through this manager. There is no remote shutdown RPC in the existing service. A console connection does not adopt an existing server. Sessions on an external server remain attached until explicitly detached.

Console commands

text
server start
server status
attach 12345
sessions
use SESSION_ID
symbols --filter Calculator --limit 20
symbols --module my_application
probe resolve "Calculator::add(int, int)"
probe inject "Calculator::add(int, int)" --callback interceptor.cpp --stack 24
events --count 10 --after 0 --timeout 20
events --name "Calculator::multiply(int, int) const" --count 4 --timeout 10
events --name snapshot --name finished --timeout 20
collect
record capture.pb 1000 --timeout 60
probe remove PROBE_ID
detach
server stop
help probe inject
help events
help server start
help colors
help !
! pwd
! ls -l /usr/local/share/clang-tracer/examples/cpp-interceptors
exit

attach selects the returned session. Probe commands operate on that selected session. Stream commands default to the selected session, or all sessions if none is selected; repeated --session ID overrides the selection. help lists commands; help COMMAND shows detailed usage, options, defaults and examples. Use help probe or help server for a command group, and Tab to complete help topics. Quote selectors and paths containing spaces; both quote styles and escaped quotes are supported. # begins a comment outside a quoted value. symbols lists functions and methods for the selected session. Use --filter, --module, and --limit to narrow a page; the console prints a complete next-page command when more results are available. help symbols explains all options. Use repeatable --name NAME on events, collect, or record to select emitted event names or full C++ function signatures with the same matching rules as the Python API. The function name is displayed with each trace event. events and bare collect have no default deadline and run until Ctrl-C. collect COUNT runs until COUNT matching events arrive or Ctrl-C. Set --timeout SECONDS to add a total deadline. Ctrl-C clears input or cancels a live operation and returns to the prompt. EOF, exit and quit leave the console.

An explicit ! prefix executes the rest of the line with /bin/sh on the console's host, using its current directory, environment and terminal streams. Shell quoting, pipes, redirects, variable expansion and shell comments retain their usual meaning. For example:

text
! printf '%s\n' 'hello console' | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'

The shell runs as a child process, so ! cd /tmp and ! export NAME=value do not change later console commands. A failed shell command reports its exit status and returns to the prompt. Ctrl-C interrupts the shell command while a server managed by the console remains running. Invalid tracer commands produce a command error; they are never implicitly executed by a shell.

Commands, help text and trace results use colors; shell input also receives syntax highlighting. Configure console colors at launch:

sh
clang-tracer-console --color auto    # detect terminal support; honor NO_COLOR
clang-tracer-console --color always  # explicitly enable colors
clang-tracer-console --color never   # explicitly disable colors

Shell programs control their own output colors independently.

Console results use readable summaries for server status, sessions and probes. Trace events show PRE/POST phase and call identifiers, named arguments, captured object fields, return values when present, and stack frames. Drop counters and capture problems remain visible. The Python API still returns complete generated Protobuf messages; this display formatting changes neither the API nor recordings.

Development

sh
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e './python[dev]'
.venv/bin/python python/scripts/generate_proto.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -c python/pyproject.toml python/tests
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check python
.venv/bin/python -m mypy --config-file python/pyproject.toml --strict python/src/clang_tracer
.venv/bin/python -m build python
# Also run the native Python integration tests after building the server/fixtures:
CLANG_TRACER_NATIVE_BUILD="$PWD/build" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -c python/pyproject.toml python/tests

Generated .py and .pyi bindings are checked in so installation does not need protoc or a native build. Regenerate with the pinned grpcio-tools version after changing either schema. The grammar and typing marker are wheel data.

The Python tests use a real gRPC transport peer to verify control requests, binary events, cancellation, deadlines and console behavior. They do not prove native ptrace injection or target restoration unless CLANG_TRACER_NATIVE_BUILD is set. That opt-in adds actual server launch, free-function and method injection, stack/event capture, recording, removal, detach, and restoration of a live probe during server shutdown followed by reattachment. Native server tests require the Linux toolchain and a rebuilt server. Process error paths also use controlled child-process doubles.

Implementation references: Python gRPC, Lark API, and prompt-toolkit.

Python API examples

Run the installed examples

On linux-dev, the installed API interpreter and examples can be used without a source checkout. The target is compiled from the installed C++ example source:

sh
TRACER_PYTHON="$HOME/.local/share/uv/tools/clang-tracer-client/bin/python"
TRACER_EXAMPLES=/usr/local/share/clang-tracer/examples
TRACER_RUN=$(mktemp -d /tmp/clang-tracer-example.XXXXXX)
clang++ -std=c++20 -g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fcf-protection=none \
  "$TRACER_EXAMPLES/cpp-interceptors/target.cpp" -o "$TRACER_RUN/target"
"$TRACER_RUN/target" >"$TRACER_RUN/target.log" 2>&1 &
target_pid=$!
stop_target() {
  kill -TERM "$target_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$target_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap stop_target EXIT
"$TRACER_PYTHON" "$TRACER_EXAMPLES/python/trace.py" "$target_pid"
"$TRACER_PYTHON" "$TRACER_EXAMPLES/python/stream.py" "$target_pid"
"$TRACER_PYTHON" "$TRACER_EXAMPLES/python/record.py" \
  "$target_pid" "$TRACER_RUN/capture.pb"
kill -TERM "$target_pid"
wait "$target_pid"
trap - EXIT
"$TRACER_PYTHON" "$TRACER_EXAMPLES/python/server_lifecycle.py"

Use your own client environment's Python if it was installed elsewhere. Native server/agent discovery uses the existing installation and PATH. The fresh run directory contains the target output and recorded traces for inspection.

Run from a source checkout

Run these commands from the repository root on Linux x86-64, after configuring the native build as described in the root README.

sh
cmake --build build -j4 --target \
  clang-tracer-server clang_tracer_agent cpp-interceptors-target

On linux-dev, use the installed client interpreter:

sh
TRACER_PYTHON=/home/husam/.local/share/uv/tools/clang-tracer-client/bin/python
export PATH="$PWD/build:$PATH"
target_log=$(mktemp)
./build/cpp-interceptors-target >"$target_log" 2>&1 &
target_pid=$!
stop_target() {
  kill -TERM "$target_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$target_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap stop_target EXIT
"$TRACER_PYTHON" examples/python/trace.py "$target_pid"
"$TRACER_PYTHON" examples/python/trace.py "$target_pid" \
  --selector 'Calculator::multiply(int, int) const' \
  --callback examples/cpp-interceptors/method.cpp
"$TRACER_PYTHON" examples/python/stream.py "$target_pid" --count 6
"$TRACER_PYTHON" examples/python/record.py "$target_pid" "$target_log.pb" --count 6
kill -TERM "$target_pid"
wait "$target_pid"
trap - EXIT
"$TRACER_PYTHON" examples/python/server_lifecycle.py

Elsewhere, create a virtual environment and install the Python client before running the same scripts:

sh
python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install ./python
TRACER_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python

Each PID example starts a local server through Client.start_server() when --endpoint is omitted; the server and agent must be discoverable from the native build or installation, and clang-tracer-server must be on PATH. Pass either --endpoint unix:///absolute/path/control.sock or --endpoint 127.0.0.1:50051 to use an already-running server. That server must be built from a revision supporting ResolveProbe. The examples attach only the target PID they receive and remove their probe and detach in cleanup. trace.py prints event sequence, PRE/POST phase, call correlation, typed argument and result values, and captured receiver fields. stream.py prints native stack functions and the advancing resume cursor, and cancels its stream at the count. stream.py and record.py also accept --selector and --callback for the method example. record.py creates its output exclusively, then validates and displays the length-prefixed Protobuf events. server_lifecycle.py shows managed process state, client readiness/session listing and graceful SIGTERM shutdown. Event counts depend on the target's call rate and include PRE and POST events.

On a graceful-shutdown timeout, an owned server's private directory is retained until it exits; the script reports its PID and endpoint for recovery. Normal completion removes the temporary directory.

The manual validation notes record observed Linux API results and example executions; addresses, PIDs, session IDs and counters vary.
